findings.title: [P1] Define `renderError` before the new catch relies on it
findings.body: The diff's entire new behavior depends on `this.renderError(error)`, but `renderError` is defined nowhere in the repository (repo-wide grep finds only this call site; `src/search.ts` is the repo's only source file). As shipped, every failed search re-enters the catch and throws `TypeError: this.renderError is not a function`, masking the original failure — the handler is guaranteed broken on its first realistic invocation. In TypeScript this is also a new `TS2339`-style reference (the pre-existing `api`/`render`/`active` elisions are unchanged by this PR; this reference is newly introduced). If the method exists in an out-of-repo implementation this fixture elides, that should be confirmed; otherwise it must be added.

findings.title: [P1] Exclude superseded/aborted requests from the error path
findings.body: Each `search()` call aborts the previous controller, so when the API honors the signal the superseded `await this.api.search(...)` rejects with an `AbortError` — and the new catch routes that rejection into `renderError`. Under completely ordinary conditions (a second search while the first is in flight, e.g. typeahead — the exact scenario the abort-and-replace pattern exists for), every superseded query now renders a user-visible failure, and a late-delivered stale rejection can overwrite a newer successful render because there is no staleness/identity check (e.g. comparing against the still-active controller or checking `error.name === 'AbortError'`). Pre-PR, aborted requests never rendered an error state; this user-facing regression is introduced by the diff. It also causes needless error-render churn on every keystroke-driven supersede.

findings.title: [P2] Catch changes `search()`'s rejection contract to fulfillment
findings.body: Before this PR, an `api.search` rejection propagated to `search()`'s caller. Once `renderError` exists and returns normally, every failure now fulfills `search()` with `undefined`, so any caller awaiting or chaining `search()` will proceed as if the search succeeded, losing the ability to detect failure, log it, or retry. No in-repo callers exist to prove a concrete breakage today, but the public async contract of the changed method is objectively altered by this diff; either rethrow after rendering (`catch (error) { this.renderError(error); throw error; }`) or document the swallow as intentional.

findings.title: [P3] Keep renderer exceptions out of the request-error handler
findings.body: `this.render(result)` sits inside the new `try` block, so an exception thrown by `render` — a UI/programming bug, not a search failure — is misclassified and dispatched to `renderError`, then swallowed. A result that makes `render` throw can leave conflicting UI state while the real defect is masked as a search error. Wrapping only the awaited request (narrowing the `try` to the `await` line) keeps the error taxonomy honest.

findings.title: [P3] Sanitize rejection values before rendering to the UI
findings.body: The catch forwards the raw rejection value to the UI renderer with no normalization or redaction. If `api.search` rejections carry stack traces, internal endpoints, or backend messages, those details become displayable to end users. Rendering a fixed/generic message (or an allowlisted one) and logging the original error privately is the safer default for this newly introduced path.

findings.title: [P3] Add coverage for the new rejection path
findings.body: The repository contains no tests at all, so the new behavior — error rendering, abort handling, and the swallow semantics above — ships with zero regression coverage. At minimum, tests should pin down: a genuine failure calls `renderError`, a superseded (aborted) request does not, and `search()`'s resulting promise state.
